findings.reason: the node would either fail its own gate or invent a predicate the deliverable does not name, and would have to touch `routing.py`/`recovery_review_subject.py`, which its write paths exclude; the deliverable must name the composite owner to work.
findings.text: §3 says `_node_is_a_reviewer` is "the TaskNode-shaped owner" of "is this node a reviewer" and infers that delegating to it also recognises a review node by its minted id, but `reckon/crew/reports.py:1831-1833` is `return str(node.role or "").strip() == REVIEW_ROLE` and nothing else. Measured in this worktree: for a node with a `REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX` id and `role='implement'`, `_node_is_a_reviewer` returns `False` while `_is_review_node({'node': {'id': ...}})` returns `True`. The minted-id question is owned by `recovery_review_subject._is_review_node`, composed with a role test in `routing._plan_review_exempt` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2465-2483`), not by `_node_is_a_reviewer`. So the deliverable as written reproduces the inline comparison exactly (a no-op), and the done-when case it is meant to satisfy — a minted-id reviewer with another role getting no readiness ref — cannot pass.

findings.reason: without a control that can differ, §3's gate cannot demonstrate the exemption is enforced at all; the section needs a control that flips on the identity route it claims to add (e.g. a minted-id node whose role is not `REVIEW_ROLE`, checked against a role-only predicate).
findings.text: the negative control "restoring the inline role comparison makes that case receive the readiness ref" cannot distinguish the two arms: `_node_is_a_reviewer` evaluates `str(node.role or "").strip() == REVIEW_ROLE`, the identical expression §2's run wrote inline, so restoring one and keeping the other produce the same verdict for every node. A control whose two arms are the same predicate passes without showing the guard fires.

findings.reason: the plan should declare §3 dependent on §2 (or fold the deduplication into §2), otherwise admission can release §3 against code it cannot see and the two sections collide on one write path.
findings.text: §3 has no declared wait on §2, but at this tree's head `_needs_own_section_verdict` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3066`) carries no role test at all: the inline comparison §3 exists to replace is present only in §2's run head `d7ab26d178`, which is not an ancestor of `HEAD` (verified: `merge-base --is-ancestor` returns non-zero). §2 is declared `implementable` with its build followup `f-arrwonpd-001` open, and the plan declares no `plan-section-depends-on` (the convention used by e.g. `docs/plans/a-coordinator-sees-the-board.html`). Dispatched before §2 lands, §3 has nothing to convert, so it must either re-implement §2's change or no-op — on the same file and the same test file §2 writes.
